definitions.cost: Provider-adjustable estimate of dollars per completed task using the benchmark trajectory's observed token mix and completion rate.
definitions.online_response_latency: Time to first token plus expected visible output generation time from LiteLLM's live observations.
definitions.quality: Mean LiveBench subtask score within the inferred complexity bucket.
definitions.quality_lower_bound: Mean subtask score minus 1.96 standard errors, floored at zero.
definitions.task_completion_speed: Terminal-Bench expected wall-clock time to a successful task, including failed attempts.

limitations: The snapshot is an offline prior; it does not replace live endpoint health or deployment latency routing.
Terminal-Bench duration is full agent-task wall time and is only compared inside the same agent/version cohort.
Trivial and simple requests require online response-latency evidence; long-horizon benchmark time is never used to rank them.
A reference speed route anchors on the cohort containing the highest-quality measured candidate; it never compares raw seconds across cohorts.
When no quality-admitted model has comparable speed evidence, speed and balanced routes explicitly fall back to cost.
LiveBench cost per completion treats partial benchmark credit as a fractional completion.
LiveBench input-token means are model-level, not complexity-bucket-specific; output-token means are weighted inside each bucket.
Provider-adjusted LiveBench cost scales the observed request cost by the benchmark token mix and source prices; cache discounts and non-token charges can make it approximate.
Provider-adjusted Terminal-Bench cost uses uncached input, cache-read input, and output token means; non-token tool charges are not represented.
Terminal-Bench token totals span many calls, so per-call long-context thresholds cannot be reconstructed and are not applied to trajectory totals.
Reference routes use the full benchmark catalog; LiteLLM must recompute them after intersecting with the user's configured and capability-compatible models.
Benchmark variants include their measured reasoning effort; runtime mapping must not silently claim the score for a different effort setting.
